For odd \(p\), \(N=p^2-3\) is even. Since \(N=q\cdot 10^k+r\), the parity of \(N\) is the parity of \(r\). Thus \(r\) must be even, and the only even prime is \(r=2\).

So \(N\) must end in \(2\):
\[
p^2-3\equiv 2 \pmod{10}
\]
\[
p^2\equiv 5 \pmod{10}
\]
This forces \(p=5\). Indeed, \(N=25-3=22\), which is \(2\mid 2\). The case \(p=2\) gives \(N=1\), invalid.

Therefore the only possible value is
\[
\boxed{5}
\]
